title: LedgerLine
description:
One line of `ledger.jsonl`.

`worker` is the key of the worker a line belongs to. `dla ledger merge` sets it on the
lines it copies from a slice. The slice records (`slice_started`, `slice_done`,
`slice_merged`) carry the same key in their own body; on the wire it appears once,
and reading such a line sets both.

ts.description: When the line was appended (RFC 3339, UTC).

worker.description: The worker whose slice the line came from; set by `dla ledger merge` (schema 3).

oneOf.description: Writers and removers were recorded for a finding (no state change).
A worker's slice began (first line of every `ledger.<worker>.jsonl`).
`dla ledger merge` copied lines of a slice into this ledger.
Two workers' findings are the same (site, holder): one is a duplicate of the other.
An independent verifier looked at a finding's bundle.
A finding got an archetype label (schema 6).
A finding got a structured explanation (schema 6).
`dla run reseal` re-sealed protected files after an out-of-band change (schema 6).

AnswerStatus.description: How completely a checklist item was answered.

oneOf.description: Not answerable now; carries reason and remedy.

Authority.description: How strongly a piece of evidence was obtained.

oneOf.description: Read from source or configuration without running anything.
Produced by a test or targeted experiment.

Bound.description: How a holder's size is limited.

oneOf.description: Weak keys: an entry goes when its key is collected.
Weak values: an entry goes when its value is collected.
A size limit: LRU with a size, ring, bounded channel, `maxsize=` given.
A cache decorator without a size (`lru_cache(None)`, `functools.cache`).

evidence.description: Supporting evidence; at least one unless `unresolved`.

runtime.description: The runtime an `intake.workload` answer is about. Absent: every runtime.

ContainerClass.description: What kind of thing a holder is.

oneOf.description:
A real container: map, set, list, slice, queue, deque, cache type, `sync.Map`, a
channel used as a queue.
Registry-like: named or typed as a registry, listener table or handler table.

Not a container: a scalar, a pointer or struct reassigned as a whole, a logger, a
function value, a type variable, a pool type, a literal or immutable table.

CoverageStatus.description: How much of the subject the evidence covers.

oneOf.description: Part of the subject was examined.
It is not known how much was examined.

EvidenceKind.description: The closed set of evidence kinds.

oneOf.description: A holder found by a census.
A retention path to a root.
Objects that should be dead but are not.
An experiment that separates two hypotheses.
A change made to the target to test a cause.
Files captured from a live process by an attached tool (heap dump, profile).

coverage.description: How much of the subject it covers.

raw.description: Path, relative to the run directory, of the full output.

result.description: The bounded result (serialized size at most [`MAX_RESULT_BYTES`]).

Explanation.description: Free-text explanation with its epistemic tag.

ExplanationTag.description: Whether an explanation was seen or reasoned.

Finding.description: One hypothesis about a leak and everything known about it.

also_origins.description:
Other origins that raised the same site (a DLA rule or analyzer hit and the census
entry of one site are one finding); set when an annotation joins them.

archetype.description: Assigned archetype; only `dla ledger label` changes it.

hypothesis.description: The cause this hypothesis proposes (on a sibling).

owner.description: Owning field or container on the retention path.

parent.description: Parent finding of a sibling hypothesis.

reason.description: Why unresolved or static-only; required exactly for those states.

refute_if.description: The result that would refute this hypothesis.

remedy.description: What would unblock it; non-empty whenever `reason` is set.

siblings.description: Sibling hypotheses; maintained by the ledger.

suggested_archetype.description: A tag suggesting an archetype; never filters anything.

FindingAnnotation.description:
Writers and removers found for a finding's holder, and its holder, owner, region and
site when none is recorded yet. It does not change the finding's state; the report lists
the sites under the finding.

also_origin.description:
Another origin that raised the same site (a DLA rule or analyzer hit and the census
entry of one site are one finding); the finding lists it in `also_origins`.

also_supports.description: The evidence of that other origin; it joins the finding's `supports`.

container.description: Container, registry-like, or not a container.

evidence.description:
Growth evidence that backs a change of a holder already set (schema 5): a heap-graph
`growth-series` with a passing column tied to the finding whose `holder_kind` is
`holder`.

holder.description: What holds the memory; applied only when the finding has no holder yet.

key_bounded.description: Its key type is bounded by the program (a class, an enum, a type descriptor).

literal.description: The holder is a literal or immutable table that is only read.

owner.description: Owning field or container; applied only when the finding has no owner yet.

owner_creation.description: How instances of the owner type are created, where the census can tell.

pool.description: The holder is a pool type (`sync.Pool`).

private.description: The holder cannot be named outside its file, class or package.

receiver.description: Registrations: where the receiver comes from.

region.description: Memory region; applied only when the finding has no region yet.

remover_sites.description: The remover sites, one per entry of `removers`.

removers.description: `file:line` sites that remove from the holder.

replaced_holder.description: The holder this annotation replaced; written by the ledger, an audit trail.

site.description: `file:line` of the finding; applied only when the finding has no site yet.

thread_class.description:
The owner class (the owner up to its last segment) also owns a holder of kind
`thread-local` in the census: state of a class that keeps things per thread.

unit.description:
The entry is the creation site of a unit (timer, task, goroutine, thread, handle):
the creation is the growth.

writer_sites.description: The writer sites, one per entry of `writers`.

writers.description: `file:line` sites that add to the holder.

FindingExplained.description: A structured explanation of a leak (`dla ledger explain`).

adds.description: `file:line` sites that add to the holder.

evidence.description: Evidence that shows the pairing, required with `observed`.

removal.description: What happens to the items afterwards.

FindingLabeled.description: An archetype label for a confirmed or strong finding (`dla ledger label`).

entry_sha256.description: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the archetype entry used; empty for `UNCLASSIFIED`.

note.description: Why nothing fits (`UNCLASSIFIED`) or any other note.

previous.description: The label before this line (audit trail).

region_mismatch.description: The finding's region is not among the archetype's regions (a warning, not a refusal).

satisfied.description: The met `requires` alternative and its evidence; empty for `UNCLASSIFIED`.

FindingMerged.description:
Replay semantics: the duplicate is excluded from the counts and the report's finding
list, and its supporting evidence is added to the canonical finding.

duplicate.description: The finding of another worker with the same site and holder.

oneOf.description: Left open, with a reason and a remedy.
A field of a container object.
A native handle or global reference.

IntegrityResealed.description: `dla run reseal`: protected files were changed outside `dla` and sealed again.

files.description: Protected files (names relative to the run directory) that were sealed again.

LabelSatisfied.description:
The proof a label was accepted on: the inner set of the archetype's `requires` that was
met and the evidence that met it. Replay re-checks this record and never reads `data/`.

evidence.description: Evidence records that carry those kinds.

kinds.description: Evidence kinds of the met alternative (wire spelling, e.g. `unit-count-series`).

oneOf.description: Static, package or module variable, class variable.
Created per call: local, closure, timer or task or handle creation site.

OwnerCreation.description: How instances of a holder's owner type come to exist.

oneOf.description: Created inside functions that can run many times.
Created only at start-up (initialisers and what only they call).

Receiver.description: Where a registration's receiver comes from.

oneOf.description: A local of the enclosing function: it dies with the call.
A parameter or a field: it outlives the call.
Native memory outside the managed heap.

RemovalClaim.description: What the explanation says about removal of the retained items.

oneOf.description: A search found no remover (the census is heuristic).
A remover exists and runs only under a condition.
A remover exists and uses another key.
A remover exists and is never reached.

Resolution.description: How an open item was closed.

oneOf.description: Left unresolved with a reason and a remedy.

SiteFact.description: One writer or remover site with what the syntax tree says of it.

const.description: The key is a literal or a named constant.

depth.description:
0 when the operation is on the holder itself, 1 or more when it is on an element of
it (`delete(s.updates[k], x)` and `s.updates[k][x] = v` are depth 1).

exported.description: The enclosing function is part of the public surface.

init.description:
The enclosing function is an initialiser: Go `init` or a package-level `var =`, a
constructor or factory of the owner type, a static initialiser, Python module top
level or `__init__`, JS module top level or constructor.

param.description: The inserted key or value derives from a parameter of the enclosing function.

site.description: `file:line` (project-relative); the same string as in `writers` or `removers`.

startup.description:
The site runs only at start-up: it is in an initialiser, or every caller of its
function (up to three calls up) is one. Read where the callers can be found.

startup_via.description:
When `startup` came through callers that are not initialisers themselves, the functions
on the way (the wrappers between the writer's function and the start-up statements that
call them), nearest first. Empty for a direct start-up call. A driver that calls one of
them calls the registration function through it.

thread_init.description:
The site lies in a thread-local initialiser (a function a thread-local runs for each
thread that reads it: a `withInitial` lambda or method reference, an `initialValue`
override, the `__init__` of a `threading.local` subclass), so the holder gets an entry
for every thread that reads the thread-local, and again whenever the thread-local was
cleared.

SiteKind.description: What a writer or remover site does to its holder.

oneOf.description:
Keyed write, put, computeIfAbsent, setdefault, Store, add, append, push, offer,
register.
Assigned a fresh empty container, or cleared.

SliceDone.description: The last line of a finished slice.

open.description: IDs of the slice's findings and open items that have no disposition.

SliceMerged.description: Written by `dla ledger merge` after it copied lines of a slice.

done.description: True when the merged lines include `slice_done`.

lines.description: Slice lines merged so far, in total (a re-run appends only lines after this).

sha256.description: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the slice bytes those lines occupy.

torn_tail.description: True when a torn final line was dropped.

SliceStarted.description: The first line of a worker slice.

base_seq.description:
Length of the main ledger when the slice began: the slice may cite main IDs
created by lines up to this one.

deadline.description: The worker's deadline (the run deadline when it was not registered).

runtime.description: The runtime it covers (the worker name when it was not registered).

Source.description: Where a piece of evidence came from.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of its contents, lowercase hex.

start_time.description: Process start time (platform string) to disambiguate PID reuse.

commit.description: Commit hash, or a project path when no commit is readable.

Tool.description: The backend that produced the evidence.

Transition.description: A state change of a finding.

by.description: The dla command that made the move.

evidence.description:
Evidence cited by the move: added to `contradicts` for `refuted`, to
`supports` otherwise.

from.description: State before; must match the replayed state.

Unknown.description: A question the evidence leaves open and how to answer it.

UnresolvedReason.description: Why a finding could not be resolved.

oneOf.description: The suspected path was never exercised.
No harness exists to exercise it.
The user declined a privileged step.

The time budget ran out: the deadline is near, or a command was refused for
time. Not a stand-in for any other reason.

Measured, and the measurement cannot decide: too few points, no plateau yet, a
single snapshot, or a discriminator that came back inconclusive. Only
`unresolved` takes it, and only with a measurement tied to the finding's family.

Verification.description: What an independent verifier concluded from a finding's evidence bundle alone.

agrees_holder.description: The verifier's holder is the finding's.

agrees_label.description:
The verifier's label is the finding's (schema 6); `None` when archetypes were off or
the line predates the field.

agrees_site.description: The verifier's site is the finding's (same file, line within 3), or both are none.

bundle.description: SHA-256 of the bundle manifest the verifier read.

label.description: The verifier's label: an archetype ID or `UNCLASSIFIED`.

site.description: The verifier's `file:line`, `None` when it found no site.
